chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Isa ibn Abdillah al-Amri, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) who said:
Let none of you pray whilst in him is one of the two knobs (impurities), meaning urine and excrement.

key_terms.الْعَقَدَيْنِ: the two knobs (referring to the bladder and rectum or the acts of urination and defecation)

ai.seo_question: What does 'one of the two knobs' mean in the context of prayer validity?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith via an extended chain back to Imam Ali (AS), highlighting the Prophet’s practical instruction regarding the physical impediments to valid prayer. The term 'two knobs' (al-'aqdani) metaphorically refers to the bladder and rectum, emphasizing that the presence of urine or feces—whether one is actively needing to relieve oneself or has residual impurity—invalidates the prayer due to the distraction and impurity involved.
